title: Five canonical fork points left on losing reorg branches
summary: Five heights in our canonical chain held blocks from reorg branches the network abandoned. Each height's child named a parent we no longer had. The defect was present for four months and nothing detected it until the archive audit was written.
detection: The canonical coverage audit, run for the first time, reported 5 broken parent links. No prior check covered chain ancestry.
root_cause: Reorg handling before 2026-07-30 adopted any same-height hash mismatch immediately, so transient miner races caused adoption of losing contenders. Once adopted, the original block was unrecoverable — its payload was overwritten and a Stacks node does not re-send blocks it has already delivered.
impact: Reads at those five heights returned a block the network had discarded. One height served 1,282 decoded event rows derived from the orphaned block. No archive had been published from the affected data.
fix: Each height repaired against the canonical chain and confirmed by the child block that names it
Decoded rows rebuilt for the repaired heights
Root-cause gap closed: a settled fork now stages the deposed block, so the chain can flip back
prevention: Bounded canonical audit runs nightly with alerting; every report is retained
The ingest parent-hash mismatch check is now an error with a repair pointer — it had logged all five as warnings while they happened
Fork repairs take a per-height lock after two concurrent repairs collided
verification: The audit reports complete coverage genesis to the finality boundary with zero gaps, zero broken links, and zero duplicate heights.
